fields.notes: Founder of the royal family of Kāndi, Dewan to Lord Hastings, a great devotee of Lord Caitanya. Inspired by Siddha Ṭoṭārāma (Ṭoṭā Rāmadāsa Bābājī #1553), left his estate to his grandson Lālā Bābu and went to Navadvīpa; led the identification of Gaurāṅga's house at Rāmacandrapura and there built in 1792 a temple of Govinda, Gopīnātha, Kṛṣṇa and Madana-mohana (washed away by 1821); kept a ṭola for students and fed sādhus and pilgrims (Navadvīpa-mahimā 407-408).

fields.disciples: Balavantarāo Bhaiyā Sāheb, stepbrother of the Mahārāja of Gwalior (taught bhajana)
fields.notes: Did bhajana at Rādhā-kuṇḍa after Gaura Śiromaṇi's passing, then at the chatrī of Kusuma-sarovara. Rāmakṛṣṇa Ṭhākura Bābājī sent him Balavantarāo Bhaiyā Sāheb of Gwalior to learn bhajana, who built the Rādhākāntajīu temple at Kusuma-sarovara and the Rādhākānta fund. Contemporary of Rādhāramaṇa-caraṇa dāsa Deva.

Famous in Vraja and Gauḍa for his renunciation: a wrapper, an earthen pot and a kaupīna. Once sat motionless on a Yamunā ghāṭ from three one winter afternoon until two the next; sometimes silent, sometimes wandering round Vṛndāvana. Friend of Kāminī Kumār Ghoṣ, some of whose family he cured.
